newsitem.title: FINLAND: Kone sees 1996 earnings "close to zero".
newsitem.headline: Kone sees 1996 earnings "close to zero".

text.p: Finnish elevator maker Kone Oy said in a statement on Thursday it expected the group's full-year 1996 earnings after tax to be "close to zero."
"Preliminary information shows that the group's result after taxes for 1996 will be close to zero," Kone said.
It was referring to the January-August results due for release on October 10.
"The result for 1997 is expected to improve only slightly from the current year," it added.
Full-year 1996 losses at its Italian operations would rise to "almost 200 million markka," Kone said.
In 1995, Kone's net profit after taxes was 66.9 million markka and EPS 13.67 markka.

Kone had earlier targetted a bigger 1996 profit than in 1995. The company maintained that forecast when it released its January-April results on June 7. Its four-month net profit fell to five million markka from 12 million.
In January-August, the volume of orders received was three to four percent up on the year-ago period, Kone said. "But the price level of new orders has remained poor," it said.
Problems at its Italian subsidiaries had remained difficult and the market in Italy had turned worse, it added.
Kone said the full scope of the problems hampering its Italian operations had now been worked out and measures were being taken to improve the situation.

A number of development programmes were under way throughout the group aiming at "a significant improvement in the operating result", Kone said, adding, the impact of these would become evident only later.
"The 1998 result is expected to be substantially better," Kone said.
